name: Finmo
summary: Business account and treasury platform: collect in 45+ currencies, hold 27+ and pay out to 195+ countries, with treasury management and embedded payments for larger finance teams.
best_for: startups, scale-ups and mid-market companies that collect and pay in several currencies and convert at least USD 10,000 a month on major pairs, and want one account with no monthly fee
skip_if: you need FX rates you can check on a public page before signing up, deep accounting sync, or your company is in a sanctioned or high-risk country; or your monthly conversions are small, because the 0.07% introductory margin depends on a USD 10,000 monthly minimum
honest_knock: The low FX rate is an introductory offer with strings: 12 months only, a USD 10,000 monthly conversion minimum from the fourth full month, and Singapore office hours. What you pay after that, or outside those hours, is not on a public page: Finmo says it is set per currency pair and volume at onboarding, typically 7 to 20 basis points. Treasury and Embedded are quote-only. Accounting links are limited: the Xero integration must be switched on by your account manager, and the QuickBooks integration is in beta and syncs only receivables and payables, not transactions. Finmo does not publish a country list; the licence and registration statements are Finmo's own, and we did not check them with the regulators.

pricing.notes: (read 6 November 2026 on finmo.net/pricing and the launch promotion terms) Finmo sells three things. The Business Account is free to hold: $0 to open, $0 a month, no minimum balance and unlimited user seats at no charge. You pay per transaction instead. SWIFT payouts carry a US$5 Finmo fee per transfer on supported corridors, and conversions on supported major currency pairs include a 0.07% FX margin (7 basis points) in the rate. That 0.07% is an introductory price, and the conditions matter. It runs for 12 months from the day you complete KYB. From the fourth full calendar month after you register, you must convert at least USD 10,000 equivalent each month to keep it. It only applies to conversions made Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 17:00 Singapore time, and not to Treasury, Embedded or any API access. Finmo does not publish the margins that apply after the promotion or outside those hours; it told us on 6 November 2026 that standard margins are set by currency pair and volume, are shared at onboarding and typically fall between 7 and 20 basis points (0.07% to 0.20%). That range comes from Finmo, not from a public page, and we have not verified it. Local transfer allowances depend on the payment method and your account, and payments sent through the API are priced separately. Finmo Treasury (Finmo's line: "Every bank account, one view of your cash") and Finmo Embedded ("Licensed global payments infrastructure to build on") have no public price: Finmo says pricing combines subscription and usage fees based on your banks, volumes and integration scope.

compare_with.name: Aspire
compare_with.why: another Singapore-based multi-currency business account in our dossiers. Aspire publishes its own FX schedule and a S$15 Premium plan; its Australian pricing page lists an FX rate from 0.5%, and the Australian pricing page of Airwallex lists 0.5% above interbank rates for major currencies (both read 8 November 2026). Finmo has no monthly plan at all, a 0.07% introductory margin on major pairs with the conditions above, and standard margins it told us typically fall between 0.07% and 0.20%. Compare what each charges for your actual monthly volume, currency pairs and country
